And kentucky took their show on the road to upset ole miss in oxford! (I wasn’t upset, were you?) </p><p>One of the main differences to note is how the coaches reacted to their losses. Now, I’m not saying I like him, but after the game, kirby spoke as you would want your coach to speak…took the blame for his team’s loss and praised Alabama’s team and even specific Alabama players for their talent. lane’s rebels were extremely disappointed with their loss, and he encouraged them by telling them their hurt just demonstrated how invested and committed they are, telling the press the “team was on the right track” with their attitude and abilities. Then you have pugh freeze down on the plains blaming the roster he inherited, proclaiming “the gameplan for auburn against oklahoma was one of the best he’s ever seen” (Probably would work the next nine times they played them, right?) and passing the bill to others instead of being accountable and trustworthy…not someone you want to bring <em>home</em> to meet mom.</p><p>And now…this weekend we hit the road! Alabama is at Vandy with the Commodore’s formidable quarterback who beat auburn last year when he played at New Mexico State. The boogs take a trip to athens to play some mad dogs coming off a loss and ready to seek revenge on their next opponent. Not to mention, the aubs <em>will not play at home</em> during the entire month of October. Bahahahaha…sorry pugh, but it couldn’t happen to a nicer guy. Maybe, the booger schedule seems a little unfair but tell that to georgia who still has texas on the road, ole miss on the road and tennessee at <em>home</em>. Eek, that’s tough stuff to have in one regular season when you count Alabama in the rearview mirror for them as well. Going to cry me a river for these folks in the comfort of <em>home</em> while watching our beloved Crimson Tide pound the Commodores!&nbsp;</p><p>Enjoy Week 6 (How is it Week 6 already?) and RTR!</p><p>Jackie</p><p><br></p><p><br></p><p><br></p>
